card: Makes addrman bucket address selection uniformly random across occupied slots. Currently, addrman starts scanning at a random index in a 64-slot bucket and returns the first occupied entry it hits, which heavily biases peer selection toward entries preceded by empty slots (such as 95.3% versus 4.7% in a two-address bucket). The change gathers occupied positions and samples uniformly from them, eliminating non-uniform peer sampling bias.
evidence: PR description: 'if for example only position 17 and 20 contain an address, 17 will be picked with probability 95.3% (whenever the initial position is 21..63 or 0..17) and 20 will be picked with probability 4.7% (whenever the initial position is 18..20).'
problem: When addrman samples an address from a bucket, it starts scanning from a random offset among the 64 positions until it finds an occupied entry. If occupied positions are sparse, entries following large runs of empty slots are chosen with disproportionately higher probability than others (for example, 95.3% versus 4.7% in a two-address bucket).

risk.why: A flaw in addrman sampling could degrade outbound peer diversity, impact eclipse resistance, or crash the node during address selection.

scope_notes: Small change (+10/-19) localized to addrman bucket sampling.
summary: Changes address selection within addrman buckets to sample uniformly across all occupied positions. Replaces the linear scan starting from a random bucket index with gathering occupied slots into a temporary buffer and picking uniformly among them.
